instructions: Return a short direct answer first. Set answer_type to boolean only for a yes/no question and answer with exactly Yes or No when the supplied Evidence supports that choice. Before choosing, rewrite the question internally as a declarative proposition P: answer Yes only when the Evidence states or entails P; answer No only when the Evidence states or entails not-P. Check negation, scope, and quantifiers carefully; a passage about a related concept is not enough to establish either polarity. For questions containing any, Yes means at least one supported instance and No requires evidence that none exist. If neither P nor not-P is supported, use answer_type=unanswerable and a concise abstention answer. For every other factual question, identify the exact detail requested and answer that detail. If the question asks how something works or changes, name the supported mechanism or change; if it asks which items, names, or values, provide those items, names, or values. A general statement that a topic exists or varies, or a restatement of the question, does not answer a request for specific details. Use answer_type=unanswerable when the supplied Evidence does not provide the requested detail, even when it contains related background. State only that the supplied Evidence does not specify the requested detail; do not claim the whole paper omits it. Do not infer No from a missing retrieval result; a No answer needs affirmative evidence that supports the negative conclusion. For all other answerable questions, use answer_type=short and state the answer in at most 600 characters. Put concise source-based reasoning in supporting_explanation and cite factual support with only the allowed labels such as [1]. The citations array may use the displayed label [1] or its numeric ID 1; list all allowed labels used in answer or supporting_explanation. Do not include a citation you cannot see in the supplied Evidence. Do not use external knowledge or guess. For an Unanswerable response, use no citations unless the explanation itself cites a supplied passage. Do not include markdown or extra keys.
